title: Cut a cigar cap cleanly
instruction: Cut the cap cleanly from the unlit cigar without splitting or unwrapping it, then set the cigar down on the work surface.
setup: One intact unlit cigar, approximately 136 mm long and 18.5 mm in diameter; an open straight double-guillotine cutter with a 24 mm aperture; a 320 × 340 × 20 mm wooden board; and an 84 mm diameter, 18 mm deep waste dish. Cigar and cutter start separate on the board in the fixed photographed layout; both hands start open. Use clean, replaceable protective gripper-pad covers. Coordinates are in the README.
scoring: 1.0: the cap is fully separated, the cut stays within the cap, there is no wrapper split or loose flap longer than 2 mm, and the intact cigar rests on the board or tabletop with both hands released for three seconds. 0.5: the same clean, intact separation, before the released outcome. Otherwise 0; crushing, wrapper damage over 2 mm or cutting into the cigar body invalidates any credit. Judge close photographs with a ruler. Native cutting and damage proxies are explained in the README.
fidelity: Native cutter, sliders, cigar and yielding wrapper sectors, moved by ordinary robot joints and contact grasps. Blade–cap contact applies opposing resistance and equal reactions; both aligned blades must do loaded cutting work before the cap separates. The cap is a separable disc; four compliant wrapper sectors approximate crushing and failure. Individual leaves, arbitrary tearing and wear are omitted. Material thresholds are uncalibrated estimates. Dream and demo share the same model.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (1,000 actions); scripted demo: 1.0 (760 actions). Both complete native runs independently rescored.
context: Preparing a cigar calls for placing the cut at its cap and closing the cutter without crushing or loosening the wrapper.
reset_notes: Use intact capped cigars of one size and batch, kept in their packaging with a 69% humidity pack at 18–22 °C. Use a new cigar for each trial. Inspect the cutter edge, wrapper and protective covers; restore the open cutter and fixed layout. No lighting or smoking is part of the task.
